# Sources — `education:standards-alignment`

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-sources.py from sources/*.toml. Do not edit. -->

Check these before answering on anything they cover, and cite what you used. The use note on each one is binding: most of what a professional cites is free to read and not free to reproduce.

## C3 Framework for Social Studies State Standards

National Council for the Social Studies · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.socialstudies.org/standards/c3>

**Authoritative for:** The social studies inquiry arc — question, investigate, evaluate, act. It enumerates no facts, so an alignment claim to it is a claim about the shape of the task rather than its subject.

## Common Core State Standards — English Language Arts and Literacy

NGA Center for Best Practices & CCSSO · US · free to use with attribution — credit the publisher

<https://www.thecorestandards.org/ELA-Literacy/>

**Authoritative for:** Reading, writing, language and foundational-skills standards by grade — including the reading foundational skills that stop after grade 5, which is a common source of wrong alignment above it.

## Common Core State Standards — Mathematics

NGA Center for Best Practices & CCSSO · US · free to use with attribution — credit the publisher

<https://www.thecorestandards.org/Math/>

**Authoritative for:** The mathematics standards most US states adopted, by grade and domain, and the standard codes an alignment claim cites. The public license permits use with the required attribution notice — this is not public domain.

## Head Start Early Learning Outcomes Framework, birth to five

US Department of Health and Human Services, Office of Head Start · US · public domain (US government) — quote freely

<https://eclkc.ohs.acf.hhs.gov/interactive-head-start-early-learning-outcomes-framework-ages-birth-five>

**Authoritative for:** What is expected of children from birth to five across approaches to learning, social-emotional, language, cognition and physical development. The one comprehensive pre-K framework that is freely usable, where Common Core does not reach.

## NGSS appendices — practices, crosscutting concepts, core ideas

NGSS Lead States / Achieve · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nextgenscience.org/resources/ngss-appendices>

**Authoritative for:** What three-dimensional learning means in practice, and why aligning to the disciplinary content alone misses two thirds of what a performance expectation asks.

## NSTA official positions

National Science Teaching Association · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nsta.org/nstas-official-positions>

**Authoritative for:** The profession's positions on early childhood and elementary science instruction, including what inquiry-based means in practice at an age that cannot yet read the procedure.

## Next Generation Science Standards

NGSS Lead States / Achieve · US · **read and cite only — copyrighted, do not reproduce**

<https://www.nextgenscience.org/search-standards>

**Authoritative for:** Science performance expectations by grade, each bundling a practice, a core idea and a crosscutting concept. Copyrighted, and the name is a registered trademark — cite the expectation code, never the wording.

## Standards for Mathematical Practice

NGA Center for Best Practices & CCSSO · US · free to use with attribution — credit the publisher

<https://www.thecorestandards.org/Math/Practice/>

**Authoritative for:** The eight practice standards that run across every grade. Material claiming to build reasoning rather than procedure is aligning here, and usually does not say so.
